import pandas as pd

def load_sources():
    # List all source file paths
    source_files = [
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_30/test_0.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_30/test_1.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_30/test_2.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_30/test_3.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_30/test_4.csv"
    ]
    # Load all sources into a list of DataFrames
    dfs = [pd.read_csv(f) for f in source_files]
    return dfs

def transform_and_merge(dfs):
    # All source schemas are identical and match the target schema.
    # The task is to combine all source tables into one target table.
    # Since schemas match, we can concatenate all dataframes.
    # We ensure data types are consistent and handle any minor discrepancies.

    # Concatenate all source dataframes
    combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

    # Enforce target schema data types and handle any necessary conversions

    # Target schema columns and their types:
    # ['categories': string,
    #  'commentCount': integer,
    #  'completed': boolean,
    #  'copyright': integer,
    #  'cover': string,
    #  'cover_timestamp': string,
    #  'createDate': string,
    #  'deleted': boolean,
    #  'description': string,
    #  'firstPartId': integer,
    #  'firstPublishedPart.createDate': string,
    #  'firstPublishedPart.id': integer,
    #  'id': integer,
    #  'language.id': integer,
    #  'language.name': string,
    #  'lastPublishedPart.createDate': string,
    #  'lastPublishedPart.id': integer,
    #  'length': integer,
    #  'mature': boolean,
    #  'modifyDate': string,
    #  'numParts': integer,
    #  'parts': string,
    #  'rating': integer,
    #  'readCount': integer,
    #  'tags': string,
    #  'title': string,
    #  'url': string,
    #  'user.avatar': string,
    #  'user.fullname': string,
    #  'user.name': string,
    #  'voteCount': integer]

    # Convert columns to appropriate types:

    # Categories can be string or list-like string, keep as string
    combined_df['categories'] = combined_df['categories'].astype(str)

    # Integer columns
    int_cols = [
        'commentCount', 'copyright', 'firstPartId', 'firstPublishedPart.id',
        'id', 'language.id', 'lastPublishedPart.id', 'length', 'numParts',
        'rating', 'readCount', 'voteCount'
    ]
    for col in int_cols:
        combined_df[col] = pd.to_numeric(combined_df[col], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)

    # Boolean columns
    bool_cols = ['completed', 'deleted', 'mature']
    for col in bool_cols:
        # Some sources might have bool as string or int, normalize to bool
        combined_df[col] = combined_df[col].map(lambda x: True if str(x).lower() in ['true', '1'] else False)

    # String columns (including timestamps and nested fields)
    str_cols = [
        'cover', 'cover_timestamp', 'createDate', 'description',
        'firstPublishedPart.createDate', 'language.name',
        'lastPublishedPart.createDate', 'modifyDate', 'parts',
        'tags', 'title', 'url', 'user.avatar', 'user.fullname', 'user.name'
    ]
    for col in str_cols:
        combined_df[col] = combined_df[col].astype(str).replace('nan', '')

    # Final column order as per target schema
    target_columns = [
        'categories', 'commentCount', 'completed', 'copyright', 'cover', 'cover_timestamp',
        'createDate', 'deleted', 'description', 'firstPartId', 'firstPublishedPart.createDate',
        'firstPublishedPart.id', 'id', 'language.id', 'language.name', 'lastPublishedPart.createDate',
        'lastPublishedPart.id', 'length', 'mature', 'modifyDate', 'numParts', 'parts', 'rating',
        'readCount', 'tags', 'title', 'url', 'user.avatar', 'user.fullname', 'user.name', 'voteCount'
    ]

    # Reorder columns to target schema order
    combined_df = combined_df[target_columns]

    return combined_df

def main():
    # Load all source tables
    dfs = load_sources()

    # Transform and merge into target format
    target_df = transform_and_merge(dfs)

    # Write the result to the specified path
    output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_30/target_multisource_cot.csv"
    target_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
